question: How does this repository define and validate its project-owned graph, and what boundaries prevent it from being treated as runtime or authority?
rubric: The graph is project-governance-scaffold in the project-scaffold namespace and is project-owned.
Its modes are knowledge and provenance, and its canonical sources include contracts, core, tests, and the System Atlas.
The export is derived and does not replace source truth.
Actionability and context are opt-in locators, not truth, execution proof, or authority.
Validation uses npm run validate:project-graph with the canonical Graph Engineering skill root.
Export is default-deny, and federation admission is parent-owned and remains unadmitted.

controls.graph_route: start from contracts/project-graph/export.jsonl, then use targeted source fallback

limitations: One question on one repository cannot support a general effectiveness claim.
Total model input tokens include system, prompt, and tool context; they are not source bytes.
Direct repository-operation count and model-visible source bytes were unavailable after host trace truncation.
The nested read-only benchmark lane could not open the Codex state database, so the same frozen lanes were executed as fresh top-level processes.
The repository snapshot included existing working changes and untracked files.
